meta.title: This Island Is Almost 2,000 Miles From Anywhere
meta._convention: One scene-spec JSON per script, saved alongside it as <script-name>.scenes.json. Each beat's `duration` is intentionally omitted -- build_video.js fills it in at render time from the ACTUAL measured length of that beat's generated narration WAV.
meta._note: Easter Island (Rapa Nui) is too remote/small to be part of the Chile polygon in world-atlas's 110m topology (Chile's geometry bounds stop around -66.9 to -75.6 lon, nowhere near the island's -109.35 lon) -- rendered as a gold marker on open ocean. CL highlight used only in beat 2 for mainland-Chile distance context.

beats.voText: This island's nearest inhabited neighbor is over 1,200 miles away. There's more open ocean around it than around almost anywhere else people live.
It's Easter Island, Rapa Nui, Chilean territory sitting almost 2,300 miles from mainland Chile, across open Pacific Ocean.
Its closest neighbor, Pitcairn Island, is still over 1,200 miles west, making this one of the most isolated inhabited places on Earth.
Despite the isolation, the island holds nearly 1,000 giant stone moai statues, some standing over 30 feet tall, carved centuries ago.
They were carved and moved without wheels, metal tools, or draft animals, and archaeologists still argue about exactly how it was done.
Almost 2,000 miles of open ocean in every direction, nearly 1,000 statues, and a mystery nobody's fully solved. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
